messages.subject_clean: merge of multirec-io into dev, closing in on rmr 1.3
messages.body_plain:
Hi this morning I merged multirec-io into dev, which means we are getting a step closer to 1.3.  This was done after multirec-io passed all tests, so I think dev is in a state where people who are particularly eager to reap the speed benefits should start kicking the tires. Please don't email me with "I run my program and it takes the same time as with 1.2.2" that was not the point. The point was to better support a vectorized style or programming that is the main approach to efficient R development. If you don't use the new vectorized features, you are not going to see much of a difference. The idea is that processing one record at a time in the map function is inefficient with small records. It's inefficient to parse or unserialize one small record at a time, it's harder to make use of vectorized functions in the map and so forth. Now you can process multiple records at once. You can also output multiple records in a single keyval call, using the vectorized option. There isn't much documentation for the new features yet but you can read the comments to issues #66 and can take a look at vectorized-API.R under tests in the source. There are also preliminary speed tests in the comments of that file. I also slipped in some improvements in the support of  structured data, whereby you can ask to see your data as a data.frame and not a list at different points in the API, maybe I should have held those back for a later time, but at least I wanted to take them into account as the API was being reorganized, to be more consistent. More work is needed on defining exactly what the structured conversion does and on the implementation side.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: R and rmr in Hadoop Distributed Cache?
messages.subject_clean: R and rmr in Hadoop Distributed Cache?
messages.body_plain:
Check out the branch 0-install. The problem with that branch is that it needs to create an archive of an R build for a specific location (the prefix option to ./configure). R builds, contrary to what has been stated, are not relocatable. There is a script in the package source under tools/0-install that will create the archive you need but right now it is specific to debian type linux distros and tested only on amazon ec2 ubuntu. Anyone with a little scripting and a little sysadmin skills should be able to adapt it to your needs and I would love to hear how it went and get the changes back as pull requests if possible. The plan is to have a few people expand and test this process to a number of OSes and when it is solid enough promote it to be the main deploy strategy, and make installing everywhere optional or obsolete.

Antonio

f3<-function() {
  #preallocate a list with a 2000 items
  result<-vector("list", 2000)
  i = 1
   #open file and read 1000 lines at a time
  handle <-hdfs.line.reader("/tmp/testdata/test.csv")
  content <- handle$read()
  while(length(content) != 0) {
        #convert lines from the file and add it to the list
    result[[i]]<-read.table(textConnection(content),sep=",")
        #read the next 1000 lines
        content <-handle$read()
    i <- i + 1
  }
  #create the final data.frame
  out<-do.call("rbind",result)
  #close the file
  handle$close()

}

There are a few things you could do to make the function faster:

library(plyr)
f4 <- function() {
  result <- list()
  i <- 1

  # Grab 10,000 lines at a time - my gut feeling is that 1000 is too
small
  # and your running time will be dominate by communication overhead.
You
  # might try adjusting up even further.
  handle <-hdfs.line.reader("/tmp/testdata/test.csv", 10000)
  on.exit(handle$close())  # ensure handle always closed even if error

  content <- handle$read()
  while(length(content) != 0) {

    # Generally you don't want to convert strings to factors, and it
    # makes the code slightly faster
    result[[i]] <- read.csv(textConnection(content), stringsAsFactors
= FALSE)
    content <- handle$read()

    i <- i + 1
  }

  # Use rbind.fill from plyr - this is a much faster implementation of
  # do.call(rbind)
  rbind.fill(result)
}

system.time(f4())

Also note you don't need to pre-allocate lists - unlike atomic
vectors, they are not copied when you add a new element:

x <- rnorm(1e7)
a <- list(x)
b <- x

# Adding a new element to a list doesn't require a copy
system.time(a$b <- 1)
# Adding a new element to a vector does
system.time(x[1e7 + 1] <- 1)

system.time(a[1e7 + 1] <- 1)

Hadley
